ORCA/Gaussian twins from the reference set, all run with the MO coefficients printed (ORCA `! PrintBasis
PrintMOs`; Gaussian `pop=full iop(3/33=1) iop(6/80=1) gfinput`): water (closed shell, pure d/f
functions), TiCl₄ (a transition metal with d functions) and the methyl radical (UKS, α and β orbitals).

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVPP, H₂O
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log` — Gaussian 16 twin (5D 7F)
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVP, TiCl₄
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g03_ch3_uks.out` — ORCA, UKS B3LYP/def2-TZVP, CH₃• doublet (Gaussian twin `gaussian/g03_ch3_uks.log`)

**1. Frontier orbitals of water, ORCA vs Gaussian.** `-b 2` shows HOMO−2 … HOMO+2. With only 3 atoms,
every atom/shell column is shown.

```bash
frog-mo tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log -b 2
```

* MO 4 is the HOMO (Occ 2.00): 99.36 % O p, with no H contribution. This is the out-of-plane oxygen lone pair.
* MO 5, the LUMO (+0.44 eV), is 47.90 % O s and 23.3 % on each H s: the antibonding σ*(O–H).
* MO 3 mixes O s (25.20 %) and O p (63.47 %), the in-plane lone pair with some O–H bonding.
* The two programs agree to ±0.01 %: the Gaussian 5D/7F basis functions are mapped to the same s/p/d/f
  shells as ORCA's.

**2. Metal d character in TiCl₄, with a heatmap.** `--elements Ti --orbital-type d` keeps only the Ti
d functions, and `--plot` draws them for the MOs in the window (the command is run inside the data folder
to keep the table title short).

```bash
cd tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca && frog-mo g04_ticl4.out --elements Ti --orbital-type d -b 5 --plot --dpi 150 --out-dir mo
```

```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-mo/g04_ticl4_mo.png
:alt: Ti d contribution (%) of each basis function to MOs 39–49 of TiCl₄. The HOMO (MO 44) is boxed in cyan. Each d label repeats once per contracted d function of the def2-TZVP basis.

Ti d contribution (%) of each basis function to MOs 39–49 of TiCl₄. The HOMO (MO 44) is boxed in cyan. Each d label repeats once per contracted d function of the def2-TZVP basis.
```

* The occupied MOs 42–44 (HOMO, −9.34 eV) have no Ti d (0.00 %): they are purely ligand (Cl) orbitals.
* The LUMO pair MOs 45/46 (−4.01 eV) is 76.66 % Ti d, and MOs 47–49 (−3.30 eV) 60.15 % Ti d. These are the
  empty d sets of the d⁰ metal split by the tetrahedral field (e below t₂).
* In the heatmap the e pair (45/46) is built only from d$_{z^2}$ and d$_{x^2-y^2}$ functions, and the t₂ set
  from one function each: d$_{xy}$ (47), d$_{yz}$ (48) and d$_{xz}$ (49). The pattern repeats over the
  contracted d functions of the basis.

**3. Open shell: β orbitals.** `-b 1 --beta` on both programs.

```bash
frog-mo tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g03_ch3_uks.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g03_ch3_uks.log -b 1 --beta -q
```

* The window is centred on the **α** HOMO (MO 4, the singly occupied C p orbital). In the β set MO 4 is
  empty (Occ 0.00, −2.07 eV, 99.62 % C p): it is the β partner of the unpaired electron, and MO 3 is the
  β HOMO.
* MO 3 is one of a degenerate pair of C–H bonding orbitals. ORCA and Gaussian return a different
  (equally valid) rotation within the pair, so the per-H percentages differ (34.24/8.48/8.64 vs
  0.00/25.68/25.68). The shell totals (51.36 % s, 48.55 / 48.54 % p) agree.
